pages.quiz:
FRENCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening for Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Vocabulary.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Vocabulary.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Vocabulary.

2. When practising Persuasive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Persuasive speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Persuasive speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Persuasive speaking.

3. When practising Oral expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Oral expression.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expression.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Oral expression.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Oral expression.

4. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.

5. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

6. When practising Grammar, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar.

7. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. chaise
   B. livre
   C. fenêtre
   D. porte

8. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Thank you
   B. Good night only
   C. Good morning / hello
   D. Excuse me

9. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.

10. When practising Reading for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Information.

11. When practising Listening for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Comprehension.

12. When practising Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Descriptive Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Imaginative Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Functional Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Vocabulary.

2. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive speaking.

3. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expression.

4. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar.

7. B — livre

8. C — Good morning / hello

9. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.

11. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Comprehension.

12. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Descriptive Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Imaginative Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Functional Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
